fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. They were sent to catch Jesus in His words (Mark 12:13). Pharisees, strict keepers of the law, and Herodians, who backed Herod's family, showed up with a question meant to catch Him. It's like a friend asking "Hey, quick question" while holding a clipboard and a tape recorder.

Yes, baker. Jesus says, "Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?" (Mark 12:24). Two things, and He names both in one question. The Scriptures and the power of God are what the Sadducees were missing.

Yes, baker. Jesus says, "When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven." (Mark 12:25). So the Sadducees' question about whose wife she'd be doesn't work the way they thought. No wedding, no problem.

Yes, baker. Mark 12:34 says, "When Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely, He said, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.”" The scribe had just said that loving God and loving your neighbor is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices (Mark 12:33). Jesus saw that answer as wise.
